No, that is not accurate. An EU/EFTA B permit (short-term residence permit for gainful employment) in Switzerland is typically issued for the duration of the employment contract, but it can be extended if the contract is renewed and other requirements are met. It is **not** automatically limited to one year unless the employment contract is itself for a limited period (e.g., a temporary job). 

An open-ended (indefinite) employment contract is **not required** to obtain a B permit. It can be granted for both temporary and permanent positions, provided the job is legally offered, the salary meets minimum standards, and other immigration criteria are fulfilled (e.g., no overburdening of the labor market, proper qualifications).

For the most current and precise information, always refer to the official Swiss Migration Authority (SEM) guidelines, as regulations can evolve.
